clue.text: Well beaten, having eaten as much as possible

definitions.meaning: a side that is well beaten has been thrashed, informally done for

definitions.text: having eaten as much as possible
definitions.meaning: full to bursting after a big meal

explanation.surface: Someone collapses after a huge dinner, as if beaten up by the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one informal word: soundly defeated in a contest, and gorged with food after a feast.

clue.text: All fingers and thumbs, Spielberg's work principle

parts.note: count every finger and thumb on two hands and you get ten
E.T. is the 1982 Steven Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A clumsy worker blunders through a Spielberg production, guided by some principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All fingers and thumbs' looks like the idiom for clumsy, but here it is literally a count: ten digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine or belief held as true is a guiding principle.

clue.text: Perform erotic fan dancing

indicators.note: the letters of the two words move about as if dancing into a new order

explanation.surface: A risqué cabaret act: a fan dance performed erotically.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as definition and wordplay: 'dancing' rearranges EROTIC FAN, and the clue as a whole hints at the act itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sex outside marriage is, loosely, what an erotic dance suggests performing.

clue.text: Sally supports drug supply

indicators.note: in a down entry the lower piece holds up the upper one, so the remark sits beneath the drug

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a sally is a witty remark or retort

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally backs a pharmaceutical supply chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name; it is a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide someone with the gear they need is to supply or kit them out.

clue.text: Monica dons American pants

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the American letters are worn around the tennis player

parts.note: Monica Seles was a champion tennis player of the 1990s

explanation.surface: A celebrity named Monica pulls on a pair of American trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British slang for rubbish, worthless, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang something pants is rubbish, of no worth or value at all.

clue.text: She packages fruit on the commercial front

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sits on top of the next
the word She wraps around the fruit like packaging

parts.note: taken as written
a pear is a fruit
an ad is a commercial on TV

explanation.surface: A woman wraps fruit for sale in a shop window at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading part of an attack or campaign is its front line or vanguard.

clue.text: Flower in garden I pulled up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read backwards
the answer lies inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A gardener describes yanking a bloom out of the flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the letters NIPUL found inside 'garden I pulled' into the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall garden plant with spikes of pea-like blooms, a common flower.

clue.text: Mix Patsy Cline record, "Mad at 13"

parts.note: to stir is to mix
Crazy is Patsy Cline's best-known hit song

explanation.surface: A request to remix a Patsy Cline hit, captioned with a quote.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is NICK, here meaning prison; STIR is also slang for prison, so the definition reads 'mad at being in prison'.
explanation.definitionFit: Driven to distraction by long confinement in jail, losing one's reason inside.

clue.text: Pretender finds benefit in fighting gesture

parts.note: a perk is a benefit of a job
taken as written
war is fighting
a beck is a beckoning gesture, as in 'at someone's beck and call'

explanation.surface: Someone finds an advantage in a combative hand signal.
explanation.walkthrough: Perkin Warbeck claimed the English throne in the 1490s, posing as one of the princes in the Tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifteenth-century impostor who claimed to be Richard of York and so a rival claimant to Henry VII's crown.

clue.text: Style of baking seen on the way round Chilean capital

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: en route means on the way

indicators.note: the capital, or head letter, of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cookery note from a journey, passing through the Chilean capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilean capital' suggests Santiago; it is just the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked in a pastry case is prepared in this manner, a French culinary term.

clue.text: Vivacity in conversion of priest

indicators.note: converting the word turns its letters into something new, a religious pun

explanation.surface: A lively spirit is found in a priest who has made a conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively wit and spirit, a French loanword for liveliness of mind.

clue.text: Murderer claiming acceptable, by the way, revealing activity

indicators.note: the street abbreviation stands beside the rest

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: the murderer takes the acceptable letters into himself, claiming them

parts.note: Jack the Ripper; a ripper is a murderer
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: A killer insists something is fine, mentioning in passing a revealing pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like a throwaway aside but supplies ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game in which losers remove clothing, so a game that reveals a lot of skin.

clue.text: Boy can cut

definitions.meaning: a boy's name, short for Nicholas

explanation.surface: A boy is able to do some cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a boy's name, prison (as 'can' is slang for), and a notch.
explanation.definitionFit: One word with three senses: short for Nicholas, slang for jail, and a small notch.

clue.text: Stop question, then answer

parts.note: who is a question word

explanation.surface: An instruction for a quiz: halt the questions, then give the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is a command, as to a horse, not a verb about halting questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A command to a horse or person to halt.

clue.text: Colourful New York district detailed, one of five

indicators.note: de-tailed: the district's last letter is removed

parts.note: Harlem is a district of Manhattan in New York
a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: A vibrant area of New York described in detail as one of five boroughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as described in detail, but means its tail (last letter) is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Multicoloured, like the diamond-patterned costume of the pantomime clown character.

clue.text: Plant's head succeeding manager?

indicators.note: the head comes after the manager

parts.note: a runner, one who runs something, is a manager
bean is slang for head

explanation.surface: A plant's boss succeeds the previous manager of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory; it is a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing vegetable plant grown for its long green pods.

clue.text: Fruity use of tongue and lips?

definitions.text: Fruity use of tongue and lips?

parts.words: Fruity use of tongue and lips?
parts.note: a rude noise made by blowing through the lips with the tongue out, which shares its name with a soft red fruit

explanation.definitionFit: The rude spluttering noise called a Bronx cheer shares its name with a red berry.

clue.text: See writer touring retail outlet in Iran

indicators.note: the pen travels around the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer

indicators.note: the shop is placed inside the letters for Iran

parts.note: IR is the international abbreviation for Iran
a shop is a retail outlet

explanation.surface: A tourist sees a writer touring a shop in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb but a diocese, the seat of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the diocese or office of a bishop.

clue.text: Around back of meadow, gardeners cultivated turf

indicators.note: the anagram goes around the single letter
the gardeners' letters are worked over like soil
the back of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Gardeners work the turf around the end of a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges GARDENERS, and 'Around' puts that around W, the back of 'meadow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of grassy ground, a poetic word for lawn.

clue.text: Our solutions cross Service supplied by ATS, PO box

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Our solutions cross Service supplied by ATS, PO box' is garbled OCR; the blog parses STY + X but the clue words for the pen and the definition cannot be recovered.
annotationWithheld.clue: Our solutions cross Service supplied by ATS, PO box

clue.text: Burying head of stiff, black humour in this

indicators.note: the black letters bury the letter inside them

parts.note: jet is a black mineral, so jet-black

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Gallows humour about burying a corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' is slang for a corpse, setting a funereal scene; only its first letter, S, is used, buried inside JET.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke is the thing that contains humour.

clue.text: Kyoto redeveloped as present capital …

indicators.note: the old city's letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Kyoto, the old capital, has been redeveloped into today's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Kyoto was the former Japanese capital; rearranged it gives the present one.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan's current seat of government, which replaced the old one in the 1860s.

clue.text: Barker holds book by very young American girl

indicators.note: the dog holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, which barks
taken as written
so means very

explanation.surface: A carnival barker holds a book next to a very young American girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' suggests a fairground showman; it is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenage girl of the 1940s in America who wore ankle socks and followed swing music.

clue.text: … whose money keeps me in the country

indicators.note: the money holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: following on from the previous clue, the money of Tokyo's country, Japan, is the yen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing from Tokyo: a Japanese allowance keeps the speaker living there.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 21 down, so 'whose money' is Japan's yen.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: English boy upset, given duck

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: Dave is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An English lad is upset at scoring nothing in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns E + DAVE around whole; 'duck' is a verb, to dodge, not a zero score or bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to dodge or avoid it.

clue.text: Christianity's dove caught escaping duck?

indicators.note: the letter for caught escapes from the duck

parts.note: a quacker is a playful name for a duck
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A dove, caught by Christians, escapes and turns out to be a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A dove is a pacifist; the Society of Friends is a pacifist Christian movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Society of Friends, noted for pacifism, so a peace-loving Christian.

clue.text: Northern English cape from central Italy

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
Umbria is a region of central Italy

explanation.surface: A northern Englishman's cape was bought in central Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is a county in north-west England, home of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the Lake District county in the far north-west of the country.

clue.text: Boy getting married, poor to rich, perhaps

parts.note: Antony is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young man marries his way from poverty to wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: poor is the opposite of rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of opposite meaning, such as poor against rich, are an example.

clue.text: Rapper's critic?

definitions.meaning: a door fitting used to rap for attention
someone who knocks, or runs down, others

explanation.definitionFit: A door fitting struck to announce a visitor; also slang for a carping detractor.
